findings.title: Safety contract: the allowlist passed to assertAllowlisted is an unpinned parameter; no module is named as the sole authority for the production allowlist path

source_refs.value: All live-scan target acquisition flows through `src/live/gate.ts → assertAllowlisted(url, allowlist)`
its hostname is injected into a benchmark-scoped allowlist file — the shipped `config/allowed-staging-hosts.json` is untouched

findings.rationale: The branded-type chokepoint (§4.1) makes the URL argument airtight, but the second argument — `allowlist` — is a free parameter. §10 deliberately exploits this by handing the gate a benchmark-scoped allowlist. The spec never names the single module/function that is the SOLE authority for loading the production allowlist, nor states the invariant that every non-benchmark entrypoint must source the allowlist exclusively from config/allowed-staging-hosts.json. As written, the 'structurally impossible to scan a non-allowlisted host' guarantee covers the host-membership check but not allowlist provenance: a future CLI flag (e.g. --allowlist <file>) or caller could pass a substitute allowlist array that type-checks while defeating the contract. This is the highest-value hole class per the injected framing (a path by which a non-allowlisted host becomes scannable). It is a missing pin, not a weakening of the existing contract.
findings.recommendation: Add a §4 clause pinning allowlist provenance: name the single production load path (e.g. 'src/config/load.ts is the only non-benchmark source of the allowlist, always reading config/allowed-staging-hosts.json; benchmark injection is permitted ONLY from benchmark/run.ts'), and state explicitly that no CLI flag or env var may substitute an allowlist source — matching the existing 'No override' clause (§4.3) for the gate itself.
findings.acceptance_check: The spec §4 names exactly one production allowlist-load site and states that the live CLI path has no flag/env to substitute the allowlist source; the benchmark exception is scoped to benchmark/run.ts. Confirm by locating the new clause and verifying it forbids any non-benchmark alternate allowlist source.
findings.verification: Re-read §4 after edit; confirm a provenance clause exists parallel to §4.3 No-override.
findings.fix_sketch: Insert §4.9 'Allowlist provenance': production allowlist is loaded only by src/config/load.ts from config/allowed-staging-hosts.json; no flag/env substitutes it; benchmark allowlist injection is confined to benchmark/run.ts.
findings.operator_decision_required_reason: Constrains the CLI surface (forbids an --allowlist-style override) and touches the non-negotiable safety contract, so the resolution is an operator/architecture call, not a mechanical edit.
findings.auto_apply_reason: Auto-apply disabled by default for claude-spec-review at launch; finding is architectural and touches the immutable safety contract, so the coordinator/operator must apply.

findings.title: stagingTargets[].auth.kind has no closed enum despite gating the active-scan login path
findings.rationale: §6.2 shows auth.kind with a single value 'form' but no enumeration or closure rule, whereas §6.7 vulnClass is an explicitly closed set requiring a spec amendment to extend. The auth config drives the authenticated crawl that powers IDOR/session checks (§7.3 active family), so the accepted values are load-bearing for the Zod schema. A defensible v1 default ('form' only) exists, so this is low rather than blocking, but leaving the set open invites schema drift.
findings.recommendation: State the closed set for auth.kind in §6.2 (e.g. 'form' is the only kind in v1; adding another requires a spec amendment, per the closed-set rule applied to vulnClass in §6.7), so the Zod schema author has an unambiguous enum.
findings.acceptance_check: §6.2 enumerates the permitted auth.kind values and declares whether the set is closed; confirm the enum is present and a closure statement accompanies it.
findings.verification: Re-read §6.2 after edit for an explicit auth.kind enum + closure note.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a sentence under the §6.2 TargetRegistry block: 'auth.kind ∈ { "form" } in v1 (closed set; extension requires a spec amendment).'
